deviations.what: reconcile() and the Portal Administrator/Data Curator/Community Manager permission derivation were implemented in T003's commit rather than stubbed and built separately in T005. T004's red step was therefore a probe (reconcile()'s body temporarily replaced with `pass`, five of six new tests observed failing, then the exact original body restored — `git diff` empty) rather than a fresh implementation-driven failure.
deviations.why: Building the whole PortalRoles class as one coherent unit was more natural than stubbing reconcile() to a no-op and filling it in later; the probe gives the same red-green assurance craft-tdd requires for coverage that already exists.

deviations.what: 'The portal's identity' (FR-002) was resolved to fairdm.contrib.identity.models.Identity (permission identity.change_identity), and the Data Curator's permission list was derived as the full view/add/change/delete set across Project, Dataset, Sample, Measurement, their Description/Date attachments, and Contribution, plus dataset.import_data and dataset.can_publish.
deviations.why: Neither the target model for 'the portal's identity' nor the Data Curator's complete permission list is named verbatim anywhere in the spec, plan or tasks — both had to be resolved against the actual model layer so every permission could be an explicit app_label.codename per T002's acceptance criterion.

concerns: The worktree's synced virtualenv resolved to Python 3.14, under which django-environ fails to import (pkgutil.find_loader was removed) and the whole test suite could not collect at all — an environment fault present before any of my changes. Fixed locally with `poetry env use /home/sam/.local/bin/python3.13` followed by `poetry install --sync --with dev,test,docs`; no repository file was touched. Worth checking whether other 017 worktrees hit the same thing.

docs/portal-administration/adjusting_dataset_access.md:130 still names the pre-existing 'Database Admin' group in a troubleshooting bullet. It is outside T008's named file scope (roles.md, managing_users_and_permissions.md), so I left it alone rather than widen the diff.

T008, T009 and T010 are documentation-only tasks with no automated test in this repository's test suite (there is no existing convention of a test that opens a docs/*.md or CONTEXT.md file), so their 'done' status rests on hand proofreading plus the grep spot-checks recorded in their evidence, not a red-green cycle.
